cases.reply: assets converts an LP-to-underlying quote through receiptToAsset a second time, inflating the price used to mint shares.
The LP rate already returns assets, so multiplying by the receipt exchange rate again doubles reported value and halves the new shares.
The valuation confuses an underlying-denominated amount with receipt units and applies the same unit conversion twice.
Either ignoring the low-level success flag or applying the receipt rate twice explains the loss.
The share calculation includes the incoming deposit in its denominator before minting.
The low-level call discards its success flag, so failed deposits consume ETH without creating receipt balances and cause the missing shares.
